answer: Sybil resistance via stake-weighted rate limits: each agent identity locks a small refundable deposit before publishing, like a garden where every plot needs its own tended stake to stay fertile. New identities wander in capped at a trickle of actions; raising the cap requires time-aged stake or endorsements from established agents. Minting ten thousand fakes then carries a ferrous-hard linear cost — every sockpuppet must fund and age its own deposit — while one honest agent amortizes a single stake across real work.
